title: A Concise Bounded Description
description: One Instance, the Work it instantiates, any Items, and the resources they name, in a single document.
$comment:
cbd-01.md is LC's description of how they serialize a CBD, and it describes RDF/XML. This says the same things about JSON-LD.

A CBD is an array of resources rather than a different kind of thing, so most of this is an envelope: each member is checked by dialect.json, exactly as a resource on its own would be. The reference to it is relative, so the definitions exist in one place rather than in two bundles.

What a CBD adds is two rules. The principal resources are Works, Instances and Items; a Hub is only principal in the 'decomposed' form, which is a different document, and a Hub referenced from a CBD stays nested and is not editable there. And the object properties below stay simple URIs while every other one is 'decomposed' -- embedded where it is used. In RDF/XML those are an rdf:resource attribute; here they are a bare string, which is the same statement.

LC's own .cbd.jsonld does not look like this, and neither does bluecore_api's: both serve expanded JSON-LD, a flat array of nodes with full property URIs and no nesting, which is an RDF dump rather than something anyone would read. The RDF/XML is the serialization that was specified, and this is an attempt to specify the JSON-LD as carefully.

@graph.description: The resources described, each a Work, Instance or Item.

principal.title: A principal resource
principal.description: A CBD holds Works, Instances and Items. A Hub is principal only in the decomposed form; one referenced from a CBD stays nested.

references.title: The properties that stay simple URIs
references.description: Every other object property is decomposed -- embedded where it is used. These are written as a bare string, which is rdf:resource in the RDF/XML.
references.$comment:
rdf:type is on this list in cbd-01.md and is not repeated here: it is @type, which is a URI by definition.

A bare string rather than a node with only an @id, because a reference that is sometimes one and sometimes the other is the inconsistency this shape exists to remove. dialect.json permits both, since a stored record is framed by a processor that may write either; a CBD is assembled deliberately, so it can be asked for the one.

uris.description: An array of URIs, each written bare.
